memory_update.text: DSGX should be carried forward as the strongest underfollowed public software proxy for customs, denied-party screening, and global trade compliance tied to policy-driven supply-chain shocks.

ULS should be carried forward as the US-listed TIC/certification proxy; verify whether regulatory complexity and supplier substitution are visible in segment growth rather than only generic product-testing demand.

Private Kpler appears to be a best-in-class pure-play for vessel-level commodity and maritime trade intelligence, but it is not US-listed; use it as demand validation and as a reference for what public proxies should resemble.

Spire Global is no longer a clean maritime-AIS public proxy after selling the maritime business to Kpler in April 2025; any remaining thesis must be rebuilt around retained government customers, RF/spoofing/jamming detection, or space-services data contracts.

Need a follow-up pass for US-listed origin-verification, forced-labor compliance, product traceability, customs brokerage software, and supply-chain risk analytics vendors; many pure plays may be private or embedded inside larger software/data firms.

node: Supply-chain intelligence, vessel tracking, compliance, certification, and inspection tools
summary: Layer 1B expansion finds a small set of US-listed public proxies for the shadow-beneficiary node where policy-driven supply shocks, trade-route disruption, export bans, and procurement compliance raise demand for shipment visibility, customs/origin screening, maritime data, and third-party testing/inspection/certification. The cleanest underfollowed public-market mappings are Descartes Systems for customs/global trade compliance software and UL Solutions for TIC/regulatory certification. S&P Global is the reference anchor through Panjiva, GTAS, maritime/trade data, and commodity intelligence, but it is too diversified to be the main alpha lane. Spire Global is a speculative residual-data candidate only because it divested most maritime AIS exposure to private Kpler in 2025; any surviving exposure must be verified around retained government contracts, RF data, spoofing/jamming detection, and post-sale service agreements.
